title: UFO programs hidden under the Department of Energy

tellings.quote: because I was told I think it was Chris Melon was telling me this that they hide things because anything nuclear would be national security.
SEC. 141. POLICY.—It shall be the policy of the Commission to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security.

r. The term 'Restricted Data' means all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to section 142.

plain: The claim is that secret UFO programs were hidden inside the US Department of Energy, because anything labelled nuclear is automatically treated as a matter of national security. Michels says he was told this, and thinks it was by a former Pentagon intelligence official named Chris Mellon. He does not say which law he means. If it is the Atomic Energy Act, passed by Congress on August 30, 1954, it makes it the policy of the Atomic Energy Commission, the forerunner of today's Department of Energy, 'to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security.' The act defines Restricted Data as 'all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons' and the making and use of nuclear material. That is the nuclear secrecy Michels says things are hidden behind. That UFO programs were placed under that authority is his step, which the act neither states nor excludes. If true, the government's tightest secrecy law would have been used to keep UFO work out of sight.
